eligibility_tiers.line: Dual credit lets you earn college and high school credits at the same time. If you have at least a 2.5 GPA and the approval of a parent or guardian, you can take college courses online, on campus or at your high school.

High school students who are enrolled in an Idaho public or private school, or who are homeschooled, are eligible to apply for Dual Credit if they have at least a 2.5 GPA and the approval of a parent or guardian.

Academic eligibility: Maintain a minimum high school GPA of 2.5 to participate. Students who fail or withdraw from a dual credit course will be required to pay for their next course out of pocket before Advanced Opportunities (AO) funding eligibility is restored.

per_credit_hour_charges.line: Dual Credit costs will vary depending on your residency, which classes you choose to take, and more. Idaho residents are eligible for a reduced tuition rate of $75 per credit. Out-of-state students may participate in U of I dual credit courses but are not eligible for Advanced Opportunities funding.
Funds cover up to $75 per credit.
Course fees: Lab, online or material fees. Online classes have a web fee of $35 per credit.
Summer courses: Not eligible for the $75 per credit rate
